findings.issue: 'unsophisticated' means unrefined/uncultured. غِلاظ الطبع means harsh- or coarse-TEMPERED, an accusation of cruelty rather than of lacking refinement — a different charge, and one that sits oddly between 'lazy' and the peasants who 'bring me gifts' two lines later (08_30). أجلاف carries exactly 'boorish/uncouth'.
'You made it back' carries 'survived the trip / got here against the odds', which is what sets up 11_20 'Must have sweet-talked your way in.' عدتَ is the bare fact of returning and drops that.

'No peace at last' is a deliberate inversion of the quest title 'Peace at Last' and means 'no peace in the end after all'. لا سلام أخيرًا is a word-for-word carry-over that a native reader parses as 'finally, no peace', not as the bitter echo. Whatever this resolves to must match however the quest title 'Peace at Last' was localised elsewhere — that title is outside my range, so please check the pair together rather than fixing this row alone.
Duplicate of the 02_BastardInteract row above — same English, same Arabic, same issue. Fix both together so the repeated line stays identical.

The English is impersonal — absolution awaits, full stop. The Arabic attaches an addressee suffix (بانتظارك, 'awaits YOU'). Contextually the Ovate is speaking to Eredrim so it is not wrong, but it narrows a deliberately oracular line and fixes a second-person addressee the source leaves open.
